md_description: This DAG represents the generation of metagenome-assembled genomes from marine microbial communities sampled across ocean depths and collection sites. It includes collection of marine samples, chemical and mechanical disruption, high-throughput sequencing, and computational assembly and quality assessment. The resulting data products support reconstruction and interpretation of microbial genetic makeup and ecological roles in marine ecosystems.

marine_microbial_community_sample.reasoning: I limited this node to intrinsic sample identity and origin because it is an Entity node. I included fields for collection site, ocean depth, and in situ environmental conditions since these describe what the marine sample is and where/under what conditions it was obtained. I excluded collection procedure details, disruption, sequencing, assembly, and quality metrics because those belong to downstream Process, Capture, Signal, and Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating any identifiers that would be generated at the root level or duplicated in already_generated fields, and used only metadata that downstream users need to understand the sample provenance and context.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the marine microbial community sample, assigned at collection or registry entry; use a stable string such as 'sample_001' or a cruise/LIMS accession. This identifies the sampled material itself and should not be repeated on downstream process or measurement nodes.

Name or label of the oceanic collection site where the sample originated, such as station name, cruise station code, or transect label. Record the site as designated by the sampling campaign rather than the ship or laboratory location.
Latitude of the sampling site in decimal degrees at the point of sample collection; typical marine range is -90 to 90. Record the in situ geographic position used to define provenance.
Longitude of the sampling site in decimal degrees at the point of sample collection; typical marine range is -180 to 180. Record the in situ geographic position used to define provenance.

Water column depth at which the sample was collected, in meters below sea surface; typical marine sampling range is 0 to several thousand meters. Record the depth at the moment/location of sampling, not the depth of later processing.
Broad marine environment category describing the origin of the sample. Record the habitat context at collection, not later experimental treatment.
In situ seawater temperature at the sampling location, in degrees Celsius, measured at collection or taken from concurrent field instrumentation. Typical marine values range roughly from -2 to 35.

In situ salinity of the sampled water, expressed as practical salinity units (PSU), measured at the collection point or from matched field profiling data. Typical marine values are about 30 to 40 PSU.

In situ dissolved oxygen concentration of the sampled environment, in mg/L, recorded at the time and depth of collection or from concurrent field measurements. Typical marine values vary from near 0 to about 10+ mg/L.

Date and time when the marine sample was collected, recorded in ISO 8601 format at the field collection point (for example, '2026-08-18T14:30:00Z'). This captures provenance timing of the entity, not downstream processing time.

sample_collection.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only fields that describe how the marine sample was collected and the key operational settings that affect the collected material. I focused on collection method, vessel/platform, depth targeting, volume or mass collected, and preservation/handling because these are process-level details needed to reproduce the sampling step. I excluded intrinsic sample provenance fields such as site coordinates, ocean depth, and environmental conditions because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded any downstream material, sequencing, or signal properties because those belong to later nodes. I also avoided repeating any already_generated field names or semantic equivalents.

md_schema.descr: Primary method used to collect the marine microbial sample from seawater or marine material at the field site, recorded at the time of sampling. Examples include Niskin bottle, rosette sampler, pump filtration, grab sampler, or sediment corer.
Field platform used for sample collection, such as research vessel, autonomous platform, or shore-based deployment. Record the platform that physically enabled the collection operation.

Intended water column depth for sample collection, in meters below sea surface, as set during the sampling operation. Typical marine values range from 0 to several thousand meters depending on the study design.

Volume of seawater or equivalent liquid matrix collected for the microbial sample, in liters, measured or estimated at the collection step. Typical values range from milliliters to hundreds of liters depending on the concentration strategy.

Mass of collected solid marine material, in grams, when the sample originates from sediment, biomass, or particulate material rather than liquid seawater. Record only if applicable to the collection step.

Duration of the active collection event, in minutes, measured from start to end of the sampling operation at the field site. Typical values range from a few minutes to several hours depending on the method.

Immediate preservation or stabilization method applied after collection, recorded at the end of the sampling step. Examples include flash freezing, dry ice, RNAlater, ethanol, or filtration followed by freezing.

Temperature used for short-term storage or transport immediately after collection, in degrees Celsius. Record the temperature applied at the sampling step before downstream processing, such as 4, -20, or -80.

disrupted_cell_material.reasoning: This is an Entity node describing the material state after disruption, so I included intrinsic properties of the disrupted biomass that matter for downstream extraction and library preparation. I focused on the disruption outcome: material state, biomass amount, lysis completeness, and storage/stability characteristics. I excluded the disruption protocol details themselves because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded nucleic-acid or library attributes because those belong to downstream Entity or Process nodes. I also avoided repeating already_generated collection-related provenance fields and any semantically equivalent identifiers.

md_schema.descr: Physical state of the material after disruption, recorded once the marine biomass has undergone chemical and mechanical lysis and is ready for nucleic acid extraction. Examples include slurry, pellet, lysate, or homogenized suspension.

Mass of disrupted marine biomass available after lysis, in grams, measured at the end of the disruption step. Use this to document the quantity of material carried forward to extraction or library preparation.

Estimated fraction of cells successfully disrupted by the combined chemical and mechanical treatment, expressed as a value from 0 to 1 or 0 to 100 depending on local convention. Record the estimate at the end of disruption using the study's chosen scale.

Qualitative assessment of how uniform the disrupted material appears after treatment, recorded by the operator or imaging inspection at the end of the step. Use this to capture whether the biomass is evenly disrupted or still heterogeneous.

Temperature used to hold the disrupted material before nucleic acid extraction or library preparation, in degrees Celsius. Record the actual storage condition applied immediately after disruption, such as 4, -20, or -80.

Elapsed time in hours between completion of disruption and initiation of nucleic acid extraction or next downstream preparation step. Record this interval to capture material stability before further processing.

cell_disruption.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the operational parameters of the chemical and mechanical lysis procedure. I focused on disruption method, chemical reagent, mechanical device/settings, duration, temperature, and a simple output-quality indicator because these define how the sample was transformed. I excluded sample provenance and disrupted-material properties because those belong to the upstream Entity nodes, and I excluded downstream nucleic acid or library attributes because they belong to later nodes. I also avoided repeating any already_generated fields from the collection or disrupted-material steps.

md_schema.descr: Primary chemical reagent or lysis buffer used to aid cell disruption during the marine sample lysis step, recorded at the time of processing. Examples include SDS, CTAB, lysozyme, proteinase K, or a commercial lysis buffer.

Working concentration of the chemical lysis reagent used during disruption, expressed as percent weight/volume, volume/volume, or equivalent lab convention as documented in the protocol. Record the concentration actually applied in this step.

Mechanical lysis technique used in combination with the chemical treatment to break marine microbial cells, recorded during the disruption process. Examples include bead beating, sonication, grinding, homogenization, or milling.

Configured intensity setting for the mechanical disruption device, such as rpm, amplitude, power level, or bead-beating speed, depending on instrument convention. Record the value and local unit convention used at processing time.

Total time in minutes that the marine sample was subjected to chemical and mechanical lysis, measured from start to finish of the disruption procedure. Typical values range from a few minutes to about an hour.

Temperature in degrees Celsius maintained during the cell disruption procedure, measured or controlled while lysis was performed. Typical values may range from ice-cold conditions to room temperature or controlled incubation temperatures.

Volume of lysis buffer or disruption mixture used for the sample, in milliliters, recorded at the point of setting up the disruption reaction. Typical values range from microliters to tens of milliliters depending on sample size.

Estimated percent of cells lysed by the combined chemical and mechanical disruption step, assessed after completion of the process. Use this as a process quality indicator for how effectively nucleic acids were released.

sequencing_library.reasoning: This is an Entity node describing the prepared sequencing-ready library, so I included intrinsic library properties rather than the preparation procedure or the downstream capture output. I focused on library identity, insert size, fragment size, adapter/index composition, amplification state, and library concentration because these describe what the library is and its readiness for sequencing. I excluded preparation protocol parameters, kit details, and enzymatic steps because those belong to the upstream library_preparation Process node, and I excluded sequencing platform settings and raw read properties because those belong to the downstream Capture and Signal nodes. I also avoided repeating already_generated sample, disruption, and collection fields.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the sequencing-ready DNA library derived from the marine disrupted material, assigned at library creation or in the LIMS. Use a stable string such as 'lib_001' or a run-specific accession.

Type of sequencing library prepared from the disrupted marine sample, recorded as an intrinsic property of the finalized library. Examples include metagenomic, paired-end, shotgun, or amplicon library.

Approximate insert size of the finalized DNA library in base pairs, measured after library construction and before sequencing. Typical metagenomic library inserts often range from about 150 to 1000 bp depending on the platform and protocol.

Observed fragment size of the prepared library DNA in base pairs, assessed after size selection and/or QC of the finalized library. Record the fragment length distribution representative of the sequencing-ready material.
Whether sequencing adapters are present and correctly ligated in the prepared library at the point it is deemed sequencing-ready. This is an intrinsic readiness flag for the library entity.
Indexing or barcode scheme incorporated into the sequencing-ready library, used to multiplex samples during sequencing. Examples include single index, dual index, or unique dual index.

Measured DNA concentration of the finalized sequencing library in ng/µL, typically assessed by fluorometric or similar quantification before sequencing. Typical values vary from sub-ng/µL to tens of ng/µL depending on protocol and input biomass.

Number of PCR amplification cycles used to generate the finalized library, recorded as a property of the library if amplification was applied during construction. Typical values range from 0 to about 20 cycles.
Whether the finalized library met the internal quality-control criteria for sequencing readiness at the end of library preparation. Use this as a simple acceptance indicator for the library entity.

library_preparation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the library-construction workflow parameters that define how disrupted marine material was turned into a sequencing-ready library. I focused on preparation kit/reagents, input amount, size-selection conditions, amplification settings, cleanup/purification, and a process-level QC outcome because these are the operative details needed to reproduce the preparation. I excluded intrinsic library properties such as insert size, adapter presence, concentration, and QC pass/fail because those belong to the resulting sequencing_library Entity node. I also excluded sequencing platform settings and raw data properties because those belong downstream, and I avoided repeating any already_generated collection, disruption, or library-entity fields.

md_schema.descr: Name of the library preparation kit or protocol used to convert disrupted marine material into a sequencing-ready DNA library, recorded at the time of preparation. Examples include Nextera XT, TruSeq, or a laboratory-custom protocol name.

Version or lot-specific protocol revision of the library preparation kit, if applicable, recorded during the preparation step. Use a string such as a kit version number or manufacturer revision identifier.

Amount of disrupted material input into the library preparation reaction, expressed as DNA mass in ng or as the measured nucleic-acid input used to start the process. Typical values range from picograms to hundreds of nanograms depending on protocol and sample yield.

Fragmentation approach used during library preparation to generate sequencing-compatible DNA fragments, recorded as the active processing method. Examples include enzymatic fragmentation, sonication, transposase-based fragmentation, or none if input was already fragmented.

Method used to select the final fragment size distribution during library preparation, recorded at the purification/selection stage. Examples include bead-based selection, gel extraction, or no size selection.

Target fragment size range in base pairs selected during library preparation, measured or specified during the size-selection step. Typical values depend on platform and library design and are often in the 200 to 600 bp range for metagenomic sequencing.

Amplification strategy used during library preparation, recorded if PCR or another enrichment step was applied before sequencing. Examples include PCR amplification, no-amplification, or transposase-linked amplification.
Number of PCR cycles applied during library amplification, counted during the library preparation process. Typical values range from 0 to about 20 cycles depending on input amount and protocol.

Purification or cleanup reagent used to remove enzymes, salts, and short fragments after library construction, recorded during the library preparation process. Examples include magnetic beads, spin columns, or ethanol precipitation.

Primary process-level quality-control metric used to decide whether the library preparation succeeded, recorded immediately after preparation. Examples include yield, fragment profile, or a pass/fail assessment based on internal criteria.

raw_sequencing_reads.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only properties of the raw data artefact itself: file format, size, dimensions, read layout, technical quality, and storage location. I focused on the raw sequencing outputs produced by the capture step, because downstream users need to know how the reads are stored and what technical characteristics they have. I excluded sequencing platform configuration and run parameters because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded trimming, filtering, and assembly-related fields because those belong to downstream Process and Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating any already_generated sample, library, or preparation fields.

md_schema.descr: File format of the primary sequencing output, recorded for the raw read artefact as delivered by the sequencer. Examples include FASTQ, BAM, or BCL-derived converted formats; use the format actually stored for downstream analysis.

Storage location or accessible path to the raw sequencing read file(s), recorded for the data artefact. Use a stable repository path, object-store URI, or local file path such as an S3 URI or '/data/run1/sample.fastq.gz'.
Total size of the raw sequencing read file(s) in bytes, measured after capture and storage. Typical sizes range from megabytes to terabytes depending on run scale and sequencing depth.
Number of reads contained in the raw sequencing dataset, counted in the stored primary output file. Record the total read count prior to any trimming or filtering.
Total number of nucleotide bases in the raw sequencing dataset, in base pairs, summed across all reads before filtering. Typical values depend on platform throughput and run depth.
Read structure of the raw sequencing output, describing whether data are single-end, paired-end, or another layout. Record the actual layout represented in the raw file set.
Nominal read length in base pairs for the raw sequencing output, measured from the stored reads or run specification. For paired-end data, this may represent the length of each end.

Summary statistic of base-call quality in the raw read dataset, such as mean or median Phred score, recorded for the unprocessed signal. This provides a technical quality indicator before trimming or filtering.
Simple technical QC flag indicating whether the raw read file passed minimal storage and integrity checks at the signal stage. Use this for artefact-level status, not biological quality assessment.

high_throughput_sequencer.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included the instrument configuration and run-session settings that actively controlled measurement of the prepared library. I focused on manufacturer/model, serial number, sequencing chemistry, flow cell or chip, read length, output mode, run date, and instrument-side quality indicators because these describe the capture environment and hardware used to generate the raw reads. I excluded sample, library, and raw file properties because those belong to the Entity and Signal nodes, and I excluded downstream filtering or assembly fields because those belong later in the workflow. I also avoided repeating any already_generated sequencing-read fields while keeping the capture metadata reproducible and machine-specific.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the high-throughput sequencing instrument used to measure the prepared marine metagenomic library, recorded for the capture session. Examples include Illumina, Oxford Nanopore Technologies, or PacBio.
Model name of the sequencing instrument used for the capture session, recorded at run time. Examples include NovaSeq 6000, MiSeq, NextSeq, or equivalent platform model.
Instrument serial number for the sequencing platform used in this capture session, recorded to uniquely identify the hardware instance. Use the manufacturer's serial identifier string.

Sequencing chemistry or kit used on the instrument during this capture session, recorded as the active measurement configuration. Examples include SBS v3, 2x150 paired-end chemistry, or platform-specific chemistry labels.

Flow cell or chip type loaded on the sequencing instrument for this capture session, recorded as the platform consumable that enabled sequencing. Examples include S4 flow cell, SP flow cell, or chip identifiers specific to the platform.
Operational run type selected for the sequencing session, describing the intended output mode of the capture. Typical values include single-end, paired-end, or long-read depending on the platform.
Configured read length in base pairs for the sequencing run, set on the instrument before capture begins. For paired-end runs, this may represent the length of each end such as 2x150 bp or 2x250 bp.
Date and time when the sequencing capture run started, recorded in ISO 8601 format. This marks the beginning of the measurement session for the prepared library.
Technical status of the sequencing run at completion, recorded as a capture-quality indicator. Use this to note whether the run completed successfully or ended with a platform error.
Whether the sequencing instrument passed pre-run or run-level operational quality checks for this capture session. This is an instrument-side QC flag, not a property of the reads themselves.

read_qc_reads.reasoning: This is a Signal node representing the processed read artefact after filtering, so I included only properties of the cleaned data file: format, location, size, read counts, read lengths, and technical quality metrics. I focused on post-processing artefact characteristics that a downstream assembler or analyst needs to inspect before reuse. I excluded trimming/filtering algorithm parameters because those belong to the upstream read_processing Process node, and I excluded assembly or binning outputs because those belong downstream. I also avoided repeating already_generated raw-read and sequencing-capture fields.

md_schema.descr: File format of the filtered read dataset after adapter trimming, quality filtering, and artifact removal, recorded for the processed signal artefact. Examples include FASTQ, FASTQ.GZ, or other stored read formats.

Storage location or accessible path to the filtered read file(s), recorded for the processed read artefact. Use a stable repository path, object-store URI, or local path such as '/data/processed/sample_qc.fastq.gz'.
Total size of the filtered read file(s) in bytes after read processing, measured at storage time. This helps users estimate dataset scale and confirm successful output generation.
Number of reads remaining after adapter trimming, quality filtering, and removal of obvious artifacts, counted in the processed dataset. Record the total read count available for downstream assembly.

Total number of nucleotide bases in the filtered read set, in base pairs, summed across all remaining reads after processing. Typical values depend on the initial sequencing depth and filtering stringency.
Observed read length in base pairs after processing, recorded from the cleaned read set. For paired-end data, this may represent the retained length per read end after trimming.

Percentage of reads or bases affected by adapter trimming during read processing, recorded as a technical quality metric for the processed signal. Use the study's chosen denominator consistently across samples.
Percentage of reads retained after quality filtering, recorded as a technical quality indicator for the processed read set. Typical values depend on sequencing quality and filtering thresholds.
Simple technical flag indicating whether the filtered read file passed post-processing integrity and quality checks before assembly. This is a signal-level status, not an algorithm parameter.

read_processing.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the read-cleaning workflow parameters that transform raw reads into assembly-ready reads. I focused on adapter trimming, quality thresholds, length filters, artifact removal, deduplication, and process-level yield metrics because these are the operational choices and outcomes of the cleaning step. I excluded raw and cleaned read file properties because those belong to the Signal nodes, and I excluded assembly parameters because those belong downstream. I also avoided repeating any already_generated capture, raw read, or QC read signal fields.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software used to trim adapters and clean raw reads during the read-processing step, recorded when the cleaning operation is performed. Examples include fastp, Trimmomatic, Cutadapt, or equivalent software.
Version of the trimming or read-cleaning software used during processing, recorded to support reproducibility of the cleaning step. Use the exact software version string such as 'v0.23.4'.

Adapter or primer sequence set used for trimming during read processing, recorded as the explicit sequence set configured in the cleaning workflow. Use manufacturer or project-specific adapter names or sequences.
Minimum retained read length in base pairs after trimming and filtering, set as a processing threshold before assembly. Reads shorter than this value are removed during read cleaning.

Minimum acceptable per-base quality score used in read filtering during processing, recorded as the configured threshold. Typical values often fall in the Phred 15 to 30 range depending on study stringency.

Maximum allowed fraction of ambiguous bases (e.g., N) permitted in a read during processing, recorded as a cleaning threshold. Use a value between 0 and 1 or document the percent convention if used locally.
Whether duplicate reads were removed during read processing, recorded as a process configuration flag. Set true if deduplication was applied before assembly, otherwise false.

Whether a contamination-screening step was applied to remove non-target reads during processing, recorded as part of the read-cleaning workflow. This may include filtering against host or known contaminant databases.

Percentage of raw reads or bases retained after the read-processing step, recorded as a process-level output quality indicator. Use a consistent denominator across the project and report the retained fraction at completion of cleaning.

metagenome_assembly.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the assembly workflow parameters that control how filtered reads were turned into contigs and genome-scale fragments. I focused on assembler identity and version, k-mer or graph settings, minimum contig length, coassembly status, input read count, and assembly output quality indicators because these describe the computational transformation itself. I excluded contig file properties and contig dimensions because those belong to the downstream assembled_contigs Derivative node, and I excluded read-processing and binning details because they belong upstream or downstream. I also avoided repeating any already_generated fields from the sample, sequencing, and read-processing steps.

md_schema.descr: Name of the genome assembly software used to assemble marine metagenomic reads into contigs, recorded at the time the assembly process is run. Examples include MEGAHIT, metaSPAdes, IDBA-UD, or equivalent assembler names.
Version of the assembly software used for metagenome assembly, recorded to support reproducibility of the computational step. Use the exact version string such as 'v1.2.9'.
K-mer size range or set used by the assembler during metagenome assembly, recorded as configured in the assembly process. Examples include a single k-mer or a range such as 21,33,55,77.
Minimum contig length in base pairs retained by the assembler or post-assembly filtering step, recorded as an assembly threshold. Typical values range from 500 to 2500 bp depending on analysis goals.
Whether reads from multiple samples were combined into a single assembly run, recorded as a process configuration flag. Set true for coassembly and false for sample-specific assembly.
Number of cleaned reads supplied to the assembly software, counted at the start of the assembly process. Use the processed-read count entering the assembler, not the raw sequencing count.

Assembly N50 value in base pairs, calculated at the end of the assembly process as a summary quality indicator for the contig set. Typical values vary widely with community complexity and sequencing depth.
Total assembled sequence length in base pairs produced by the metagenome assembly process, measured at completion. This is a process-level output metric summarizing the scale of assembled sequence.
Completion status of the assembly process, indicating whether the computational run finished successfully or encountered issues. Use a categorical status to support workflow traceability.

assembled_contigs.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only properties of the computed contig set itself: file representation, contig counts, lengths, assembly statistics, and sequence-level quality metrics. I focused on what a downstream binning or analysis user needs to know about the assembled sequence artefact, rather than how the assembly was performed. I excluded assembler software and k-mer settings because those belong to the upstream metagenome_assembly Process node, and I excluded raw read and capture details because those are upstream Signal/Capture nodes. I also avoided repeating any already_generated assembly-process fields.

md_schema.descr: File format of the assembled contig dataset, recorded for the computed derivative artefact. Examples include FASTA, FASTA.GZ, or other stored sequence formats used for downstream binning and analysis.

Storage location or accessible path to the assembled contig file, recorded for the derivative artefact. Use a stable repository path, object-store URI, or local file path such as '/data/assembly/contigs.fasta.gz'.
Total number of contigs produced by the assembly, counted in the final computed sequence set. Record the count after any contig-length filtering applied to the derivative artefact.
Contig N50 in base pairs, calculated from the final contig set as a standard assembly statistic. This summarizes contiguity of the derivative output and is typically reported at the end of assembly.
Length in base pairs of the longest contig in the assembled set, measured from the final derivative output. This provides a simple upper-bound statistic for assembly contiguity.
Total length in base pairs of all contigs in the assembly, summed across the final computed derivative output. This indicates the total reconstructed sequence content.
Mean or aggregate GC content of the assembled contigs, expressed as a percentage, measured from the derivative sequence set. Use the project’s chosen summary statistic consistently across samples.
Summary of read coverage across the assembled contigs, recorded as a derivative-level quality indicator. This may be a mean, median, or distribution summary depending on the study convention.

Optional sequence-level proxy for the completeness of the contig set, recorded if assessed directly from the assembly output. Use a computed metric or textual summary that reflects how much of the metagenome appears to be reconstructed.

genome_binning.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the binning workflow parameters that describe how assembled contigs were grouped into MAG bins. I focused on binning software identity and version, input contig thresholds, coverage/tetranucleotide usage, number of bins targeted, and process-level binning yield because these capture the operational choices and outcomes of the grouping step. I excluded properties of the resulting MAGs such as bin completeness or contamination because those belong to the downstream metagenome_assembled_genomes Entity and quality assessment nodes. I also excluded contig file properties and assembly settings because those belong upstream, and I avoided repeating already_generated assembly and contig fields.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software used to group assembled contigs into genome bins, recorded at the time the binning process was run. Examples include MetaBAT2, MaxBin2, CONCOCT, or equivalent binning tools.
Version of the binning software used for the genome binning step, recorded to support reproducibility of the process. Use the exact version string such as 'v2.15'.

Primary binning strategy applied to cluster contigs into putative genomes, recorded as the operational method used by the process. Examples include coverage-based, composition-based, or hybrid binning.
Minimum contig length in base pairs required for inclusion in the binning process, recorded as a binning threshold. Typical values often range from 1000 to 2500 bp depending on the pipeline.

Whether coverage information across samples or runs was used as an input feature for binning, recorded as a process configuration flag. This indicates whether abundance information informed the clustering step.

Whether tetranucleotide or k-mer composition profiles were used as an input feature for binning, recorded as a process configuration flag. This indicates whether sequence composition informed the clustering step.
Approximate number of genome bins expected or requested from the binning process, if such a target was configured. Record the intended binning output scale rather than the final bin count.

Percentage of assembled contigs or assembly length retained in genome bins after clustering, recorded as a process-level output quality indicator. Use a consistent denominator defined by the binning workflow.

Completion status of the genome binning process, indicating whether the computational clustering finished successfully or encountered issues. Use a categorical status to support workflow traceability.

metagenome_assembled_genomes.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only properties of the computed MAG bin set itself: bin identifiers, file locations, counts, size and N50 statistics, GC content, and aggregate completeness/contamination summaries. These fields describe the derived genome bins as an artefact and provide the minimum information needed for reuse and interpretation. I excluded binning software parameters because those belong to the upstream genome_binning Process node, and I excluded detailed quality assessment metrics because those belong to the downstream mag_quality_assessment and quality_metrics nodes. I also avoided repeating already_generated assembly, contig, and binning process fields.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the set of metagenome-assembled genomes produced from the marine assembly, assigned to the derived MAG collection. Use a stable string such as 'mag_set_001' or a project accession.
File format of the MAG bin sequences or bin collection, recorded for the derivative artefact. Examples include FASTA, FASTA.GZ, or archive formats used to distribute bin sequences.

Storage location or accessible path to the MAG sequence file(s), recorded for the derivative artefact. Use a stable repository path, object-store URI, or local file path such as '/data/mags/bin_001.fasta.gz'.
Total number of MAG bins recovered from the marine assembly, counted in the final derivative set. Record the number of bins available for downstream quality assessment and analysis.
Minimum genome length in base pairs among the recovered MAG bins, measured from the final derived set. This helps characterize the size distribution of recovered genomes.
Maximum genome length in base pairs among the recovered MAG bins, measured from the final derived set. This helps summarize the range of bin sizes recovered.
N50 statistic in base pairs for the MAG collection, calculated from the final derived genome bins. This provides a standard summary of contiguity or size distribution within the MAG set.
Mean GC content of the recovered MAG bins, expressed as a percentage, measured from the derived genome set. Use the same summary convention across samples for comparability.

Summary completeness estimate for the MAG set, expressed as a percentage or as an aggregate statistic across bins, recorded from the derived output. Use this as a high-level indicator of how complete the recovered genomes are.

Summary contamination estimate for the MAG set, expressed as a percentage or as an aggregate statistic across bins, recorded from the derived output. Use this as a high-level indicator of purity of the recovered genomes.

mag_quality_assessment.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the quality-assessment workflow parameters and outputs that describe how the MAG bins were evaluated. I focused on the assessment tool, version, reference database, thresholds for completeness and contamination, and the resulting pass/fail or category assignment because these define the operation and its acceptance criteria. I excluded the MAG bin properties themselves because those belong to the downstream quality_metrics Derivative node, and I excluded assembly or binning settings because those belong upstream. I also avoided repeating already_generated MAG collection fields and kept the schema centered on the assessment step only.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software used to evaluate the quality of the MAG bins, recorded at the time the assessment process was run. Examples include CheckM2, BUSCO, GTDB-Tk quality checks, or equivalent tools.
Version of the MAG quality-assessment software used for the evaluation step, recorded to support reproducibility of the process. Use the exact version string such as 'v1.0.2'.

Reference database or marker set used by the quality assessment tool to estimate completeness and contamination, recorded during the assessment process. Examples include lineage-specific marker sets or curated genome databases.

Minimum completeness percentage required for a MAG to pass the quality assessment, configured as the acceptance threshold for the process. Typical values are often around 50, 70, or 90 percent depending on intended genome quality class.

Maximum contamination percentage allowed for a MAG to pass the quality assessment, configured as the acceptance threshold for the process. Typical values are often around 5 to 10 percent depending on quality requirements.
Categorical scheme used to classify MAG quality during assessment, recorded at the end of the process. Examples include high_quality, medium_quality, low_quality, or custom project categories.
Number of MAG bins that passed the quality assessment thresholds, counted at completion of the evaluation process. This is a process-level output metric summarizing the number of acceptable genomes.
Completion status of the MAG quality-assessment process, indicating whether the evaluation finished successfully or encountered issues. Use a categorical status to support workflow traceability.

quality_metrics.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed quality-result properties of the MAG assessment output itself: per-bin identifiers, completeness, contamination, strain heterogeneity, quality score/class, and pass/fail flags. These fields describe the derived metric table that downstream users will inspect or filter on. I excluded the assessment software, databases, and thresholds because those belong to the upstream mag_quality_assessment Process node, and I excluded bin sequence properties because those belong to the metagenome_assembled_genomes Derivative node. I also avoided repeating already_generated MAG collection or assessment-process fields.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed MAG quality-metrics table or record set, assigned to the derivative output of the assessment workflow. Use a stable string such as 'quality_metrics_001' or a project accession.

Identifier of the MAG bin to which the computed quality metrics apply, matching the corresponding bin identifier in the recovered MAG set. Use the same bin label used throughout the workflow, such as 'bin_01'.

Estimated genome completeness percentage for the MAG bin, computed from the quality assessment results. Typical values range from 0 to 100 and indicate how much of the expected genome content is recovered.
Estimated contamination percentage for the MAG bin, computed from the quality assessment results. Typical values range from 0 upward, with lower values indicating cleaner bins.

Estimated strain heterogeneity percentage for the MAG bin, if reported by the quality assessment method, computed as part of the derivative output. Use the project’s chosen scale and summary convention.

Composite quality score assigned to the MAG bin by the assessment workflow or post-processing rules, recorded as a derivative metric. Use the score definition employed in the project, such as a numeric ranking or normalized score.

Categorical quality label assigned to the MAG bin based on computed completeness and contamination results, recorded in the derivative output. Typical labels may distinguish high-quality, medium-quality, and lower-quality bins.

Whether the MAG bin meets the downstream quality filter criteria after applying the computed assessment metrics, recorded as a derivative-level boolean. This is the final acceptance flag for reuse in interpretation or reporting.

marine_ecological_analysis.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the computational/interpretive analysis parameters that describe how quality-checked MAGs were used to infer ecological roles. I focused on analysis software, version, reference databases, functional annotation strategy, taxonomy assignment, environmental stratification, and a process-level outcome indicator because these are the operation-level choices and results. I excluded the interpreted results themselves because those belong to the downstream ecological_interpretation Derivative node, and I excluded MAG quality, bin, or assembly details because those belong upstream. I also avoided repeating already_generated assessment and MAG fields.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or analysis pipeline used to interpret quality-checked MAGs for ecological and functional roles, recorded at the time the process was run. Examples include DRAM, Prokka, KEGG annotation workflows, or custom analysis pipelines.
Version of the ecological analysis software or pipeline used for MAG interpretation, recorded to support reproducibility of the process. Use the exact version string such as 'v1.5.0'.

Reference database used to infer gene functions, pathways, or ecological traits from the MAGs during analysis, recorded as part of the interpretive process. Examples include KEGG, eggNOG, Pfam, or custom marine gene databases.

Method used to assign taxonomy to the MAGs during ecological analysis, recorded as the active interpretive approach. Examples include marker-gene placement, ANI-based classification, or GTDB-based assignment.

Whether the ecological analysis explicitly stratified MAG interpretation by marine environment or depth zone, recorded as a process configuration flag. Set true if depth or site categories were used in the analysis design.

Number of quality-checked MAGs supplied to the ecological analysis process, counted at the start of interpretation. Use the post-QC MAG count entering the analysis, not the total recovered before filtering.

Number of functional features, genes, or annotations identified during the ecological analysis step, recorded as a process-level output metric. This summarizes the scale of the interpretive results before they are organized into a downstream table.
Completion status of the ecological analysis process, indicating whether the interpretation finished successfully or encountered issues. Use a categorical status to support workflow traceability.

ecological_interpretation.reasoning: I corrected the derivative schema by removing the colliding field name mag_bin_id, since it was already generated in a prior DAG step and must not be repeated. I kept only fields that describe the final ecological interpretation output itself: table identifier, predicted taxonomy, functional summary, ecological role, depth association, confidence, and evidence summary. I preserved the node’s semantic territory as a Derivative by excluding upstream analysis settings and upstream MAG quality properties.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed ecological interpretation table or record set, assigned to the final derivative output. Use a stable string such as 'eco_interp_001' or a project accession.

Predicted taxonomic label assigned to the MAG in the interpretation table, recorded as the downstream summary of taxonomic identity. Examples may include genus- or species-level labels where supported.

Concise summary of the main inferred functional capabilities of the MAG, such as nutrient cycling, carbon metabolism, or stress response, recorded in the interpretation output. Use a short textual description suitable for table display.

Categorical label describing the likely ecological role inferred for the MAG in marine ecosystems, recorded in the interpretation table. Examples include primary producer, heterotroph, sulfur cycler, nitrogen cycler, or symbiont.

Categorical summary of the ocean depth zone or habitat association inferred for the MAG, recorded in the interpretation output. Use the classification applied by the analysis to describe likely environmental niche.

Numeric confidence score for the ecological interpretation assigned to the MAG, recorded as a downstream summary metric. Typical values range from 0 to 1 or 0 to 100 depending on project convention; document the chosen scale consistently.

Short textual summary of the evidence used to support the ecological interpretation, such as marker genes, pathway annotations, or taxonomy placement. This captures the basis for the computed downstream summary rather than the analytical method configuration.
